## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column must be fixed before merge: it holds the start timestamp of processes that are still running, so consumers would read running processes as finished. Its documented NULL meaning is also wrong for processes that were started and then cleared.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. The column is populated from `occurred_at` when the latest event is `started`. The pull request also adds a one-line `review.txt` file.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — finished_at holds the start time of running processes — For process 20, whose latest event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, `finished_at` comes out as that start time even though the process has not finished. `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `created`, `started` and `cleared`, so no event marks a finish. — Any consumer that filters on `finished_at` will treat every currently running process as finished at the moment it started. — Fix: Either rename the column to `started_at` and update the description at `models/schema.yml:11`, or derive a real finish timestamp from an event that marks completion.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented NULL meaning of finished_at — Process 30 is `started` and then `cleared`, so its `finished_at` is NULL, but the docs say "NULL means the process has never been started." The code `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` returns NULL whenever the latest event is anything other than `started`. — Consumers who follow the schema docs will wrongly conclude that cleared processes were never started.
